title: 📘 UNIT 6: ETHIOPIA: INTERNAL DEVELOPMENTS AND EXTERNAL INFLUENCES FROM 1941 TO 1991
6.1 🏛️ MAJOR ADMINISTRATIVE REFORMS AND SOCIO-ECONOMIC CONDITIONS
notes:
After liberation in 1941, Emperor Haile Selassie worked to restore and strengthen the central government.

🎯 Main objectives included centralization, modernization and weakening the power of regional nobility.

🌍 Ethiopia was also strongly influenced by Britain and later by the United States.

📌 Major areas of development included administration, agriculture, land tenure, trade, industry, finance, education, transport, communication and health.

title: 6.1.1 🇬🇧🇺🇸 EXTERNAL INFLUENCES
notes:
🇬🇧 British influence → Britain became highly influential in Ethiopia immediately after the defeat of Fascist Italy.

📌 British interests included military influence, strategic interests in the Horn of Africa and control of important areas around Ethiopia.

🇺🇸 American influence → The United States gradually replaced Britain as Ethiopia's major foreign supporter.

🤝 Point Four Program → promoted technical assistance, agricultural development, education and economic modernization.

⚠️ By the 1960s and 1970s, opposition to American influence increased, especially among Ethiopian students.

title: 6.1.2 🏛️ ADMINISTRATIVE REFORMS
notes:
📅 1942 → Ethiopia was reorganized into twelve governorate-generals called Teqlay Gizat.

🏛️ Each governorate was divided into awrajas, weredas and mikitil weredas.

👤 Governors were appointed by the Emperor and represented central authority in the provinces.

🎯 Purpose → strengthen central government and reduce the independent power of regional nobles.

📌 Centralization became a major feature of Haile Selassie's rule.

title: 6.1.3 📜 THE 1955 REVISED CONSTITUTION
notes:
📅 1955 → Emperor Haile Selassie introduced a revised constitution.

🏛️ Main features → strengthened the Emperor's authority, reorganized government institutions and provided for a bicameral parliament.

👑 The Emperor retained extensive powers over government, the military and administration.

📌 Significance → introduced some modern constitutional institutions while maintaining strong imperial authority.

title: 6.1.4 🌾 AGRICULTURE, LAND TENURE AND TENANCY
notes:
🌾 Agriculture → remained the foundation of Ethiopia's economy and provided employment for most of the population.

🏞️ Traditional land systems → included rist, gult and other forms of landholding and tribute collection.

👨‍🌾 Tenancy → widespread in southern Ethiopia, where many peasants cultivated land owned by landlords.

⚠️ Problems → high rents, evictions, land sales and exploitation created widespread rural poverty.

📢 Land inequality became one of the major causes of opposition to the Imperial regime.

🗣️ Student slogan → "Land to the Tiller" became a major demand of the Ethiopian student movement.

title: 6.1.5 🏭 TRADE, INDUSTRY, FINANCE, EDUCATION AND INFRASTRUCTURE
notes:
🏪 Trade and industry → expanded gradually as the government encouraged modern economic development.

🏦 Financial sector → modern banking and financial institutions expanded during the Imperial period.

🏫 Education → secondary and higher education expanded, creating a growing educated population.

🚧 Transport → roads and other transport facilities developed to connect major towns and economic centres.

📡 Communication → telephone, radio and other communication services expanded.

🏥 Health → modern medical services and health institutions gradually increased.

📌 These developments contributed to modernization but remained limited and unevenly distributed.

title: 6.1.6 🌾 FAMINE AND SOCIO-ECONOMIC CRISIS
notes:
⚠️ Rural Ethiopia suffered repeated droughts and famines during the Imperial period.

📅 Major famines affected Tigray, Wag-Lasta and Wallo at different times.

💔 Effects → death, displacement, poverty and food insecurity.

🏙️ Urban problems included inflation, unemployment and corruption.

🎥 Jonathan Dimbleby's documentary "Hidden Hunger" exposed the devastating famine in Wallo to the international community.

📌 Famine and government failure to respond effectively contributed to growing opposition against the Imperial regime.

title: 6.2 ⚔️ EARLY OPPOSITION MOVEMENTS AGAINST IMPERIAL RULE
notes:
Opposition to the Imperial regime came from several groups.

🌾 Peasants resisted taxation and land policies.

⚔️ Military officers attempted to change the political system.

🎓 Students demanded democracy, equality and social justice.

📌 These movements gradually weakened the Imperial government and contributed to the Revolution of 1974.

title: 6.2.1 🌾 PEASANT REVOLTS
notes:
👨‍🌾 Peasant rebellions were mainly caused by taxation, land problems, exploitation and interference by the central government.

📍 Important examples included the Bale uprising and the Gojjam uprising.

🌾 Gojjam revolt → intensified after the government introduced the agricultural income tax in 1967.

⚔️ Peasants resisted government tax assessors and fought government forces.

📌 Significance → peasant resistance demonstrated widespread dissatisfaction with Imperial economic and administrative policies.

title: 6.2.2 ⚔️ THE 1960 COUP ATTEMPT
notes:
📅 December 1960 → members of the Imperial Bodyguard attempted to overthrow Haile Selassie's government while he was abroad.

👥 Main leaders → General Mengistu Neway and Germame Neway.

🎯 Objectives → introduce political and economic reforms and establish a more modern government.

❌ Failure → the coup lacked sufficient military support and effective organization.

📌 Result → the Imperial government regained control and the coup leaders were defeated.

title: 6.2.3 🎓 THE ETHIOPIAN STUDENT MOVEMENT
notes:
🎓 The student movement expanded with the growth of secondary and higher education.

🏫 Its major centre was Haile Selassie I University, formerly University College of Addis Ababa.

📢 Major demands → democracy, equality, free press, better education and social justice.

🌾 Land reform → "Land to the Tiller" became one of its most famous slogans.

🌍 Students also criticized American imperialism and foreign influence.

⭐ Importance → the student movement became one of the strongest forces challenging the Imperial regime.

title: 6.3 🔥 THE ETHIOPIAN REVOLUTION OF 1974 AND FALL OF THE MONARCHY
notes:
📅 1974 → Ethiopia experienced a major political revolution that ended the Imperial monarchy.

🔥 Major causes → land inequality, economic hardship, famine, unemployment, inflation, corruption, authoritarian rule, military dissatisfaction and student opposition.

📌 The crisis spread through the military, students, workers and wider society.

👑 September 1974 → Emperor Haile Selassie was deposed.

⚔️ The military committee known as the Derg emerged as the new ruling authority.

📅 1975 → Haile Selassie died while under detention.

title: 6.3.1 ⚔️ DEPOSITION OF THE EMPEROR AND EMERGENCE OF THE DERG
notes:
🪖 Derg → a committee of military and police representatives that gradually took control of Ethiopia.

👤 Mengistu Haile Mariam eventually became its dominant leader.

🎯 Initial goal → restore order and reform the state.

📌 The Derg later adopted Marxism-Leninism and established a socialist-oriented political system.

⚠️ Political struggle developed between the Derg and revolutionary opposition groups.

title: 6.3.2 🌾 SOCIO-ECONOMIC REFORMS OF THE DERG
notes:
🌾 1975 Land Reform → rural land was nationalized and landlords lost ownership of land.

🏙️ Urban land and extra houses were also nationalized.

🏭 Major industries and financial institutions were brought under state control.

👨‍🌾 Peasant associations were established to organize rural communities.

🏘️ Urban dwellers' associations were created in towns.

📌 Goal → replace the old landholding system with a socialist economic structure.

title: 6.3.3 ☠️ RED TERROR AND POLITICAL STRUGGLE
notes:
⚔️ Political conflict intensified between the Derg and opposition groups, especially the Ethiopian People's Revolutionary Party.

☠️ Red Terror → violent campaign launched by the Derg against its political opponents, particularly in urban areas.

📅 1977–1978 → the campaign reached its most intense period.

💔 Effects → thousands of people were killed, imprisoned or displaced.

📌 By 1978, the Derg had largely suppressed organized opposition in major cities, although armed resistance continued in several regions.

title: 6.3.4 🏛️ WORKERS' PARTY AND THE PDRE
notes:
📅 1984 → Workers' Party of Ethiopia was established as the ruling political party.

📜 1987 → People's Democratic Republic of Ethiopia was proclaimed.

🏛️ New constitution → established a socialist one-party state.

🗺️ The country was organized into administrative and autonomous regions.

👤 Mengistu Haile Mariam became the central political figure.

📌 Political power became concentrated in the party and state leadership.

title: 6.4 ⚔️ ETHIO-SOMALIA WAR AND FOREIGN INFLUENCES
notes:
🌍 Ethiopia's conflicts during the Derg period were strongly influenced by the Cold War.

🇸🇴 Somalia → President Siad Barre's government claimed the Somali-inhabited Ogaden region of Ethiopia.

⚔️ 1977 → Somalia launched a major invasion of the Ogaden.

🇪🇹 Ethiopia received major military support from the Soviet Union and Cuba.

🏆 1978 → Ethiopian and allied forces defeated the Somali invasion.

📌 Result → Ethiopia retained control of the Ogaden, while the conflict strengthened Soviet influence in Ethiopia.

title: 6.4.1 ⚔️ THE ETHIO-SOMALIA WAR OF 1977
notes:
🎯 Main cause → Somalia's territorial claim over the Ogaden and its support for Somali forces operating inside Ethiopia.

🇸🇴 Somalia initially achieved major military successes.

🇪🇹 Ethiopia reorganized its forces and received large-scale assistance from the Soviet Union and Cuba.

🏆 By 1978 → Ethiopian forces and their allies had pushed Somali forces out of most of the Ogaden.

⭐ Significance → the war demonstrated the importance of Cold War alliances in the Horn of Africa.

title: 6.4.2 🇪🇷 THE QUESTION OF ERITREA AND ARMED STRUGGLE
notes:
🇪🇷 Eritrea had been federated with Ethiopia in 1952 under a UN arrangement.

📅 1962 → Emperor Haile Selassie ended the federation and incorporated Eritrea into Ethiopia.

⚔️ Armed struggle → Eritrean organizations fought for greater autonomy and eventually independence.

👥 Major organization → Eritrean Liberation Front was followed by the Eritrean People's Liberation Front.

📌 The conflict continued through the Imperial and Derg periods.

🕊️ 1991 → the Derg fell and Eritrean forces took control of Asmara.

📅 1993 → Eritrea became independent following a referendum.

title: 6.4.3 📉 FALL OF THE DERG REGIME
notes:
⚠️ The Derg faced serious internal and external problems during the 1980s.

🌾 Economic crisis → drought, famine, debt and weak economic performance.

⚔️ Armed opposition → EPLF, TPLF and other movements continued fighting the government.

🌍 External factor → the decline of Soviet support weakened the Derg's international position.

📅 1984–1985 → severe famine caused enormous human suffering and damaged the government's credibility.

⚔️ 1991 → rebel forces advanced toward Addis Ababa and the Derg regime collapsed.

📌 Mengistu left Ethiopia and went into exile in Zimbabwe.

title: 🏆 UNIT 6 — MUST REMEMBER
notes:
🇪🇹 1941 → Restoration of Ethiopian independence after Italian occupation.

🏛️ 1942 → Ethiopia reorganized into twelve governorate-generals.

📜 1955 → Revised Constitution introduced.

⚔️ 1960 → Coup attempt led by Mengistu and Germame Neway failed.

🎓 1960s → Ethiopian student movement became increasingly influential.

🌾 1967 → Agricultural income tax contributed to the Gojjam uprising.

🔥 1974 → Ethiopian Revolution ended the Imperial monarchy.

🪖 1974 → Derg emerged as the new ruling authority.

🌾 1975 → Land reform nationalized rural land and abolished landlord ownership.

☠️ 1977–1978 → Red Terror reached its most intense period.

⚔️ 1977 → Somalia invaded the Ogaden.

🏆 1978 → Ethiopian forces and allies defeated the Somali invasion.

🏛️ 1984 → Workers' Party of Ethiopia established.

🌾 1984–1985 → devastating famine affected Ethiopia.

📜 1987 → People's Democratic Republic of Ethiopia established.

⚔️ 1991 → Derg regime collapsed.

🇪🇹 BIG PICTURE → After liberation in 1941, Haile Selassie strengthened central government and pursued modernization. However, land inequality, poverty, famine, authoritarian rule and growing opposition weakened the monarchy. The Revolution of 1974 brought the Derg to power, which introduced socialist reforms and nationalized land and major industries. The regime faced political opposition, the Red Terror, the Ethio-Somalia War, Eritrean armed struggle, economic crisis and famine. Internal rebellion and declining foreign support eventually contributed to the collapse of the Derg in 1991.
